lesson.title: Code Your Own CLI With Rust
lesson.goal: build a command-line tool in Rust with cargo that parses arguments

goalMatch.note: This code-along builds a Rust CLI app using crates via cargo, which very likely includes argument parsing (e.g. clap), though the description doesn't say so explicitly.

sources.title: Code Your Own CLI With Rust

steps.title: Initialize project and add clap dependency
steps.instructions: Run `cargo new bestls && cd bestls` to create a new Rust binary project. Open Cargo.toml and add clap with the derive feature under [dependencies].

targets.caption: Cargo creates the binary package
Add the clap crate with the derive feature in Cargo.toml

explanations.topic: Purpose of clap derive feature for CLI parsing

hints: Run cargo new followed by your project name in an empty folder.
Open Cargo.toml and look under the [dependencies] section.
Add clap = { version = "4.5.39", features = ["derive"] }.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to enable features = ["derive"] on clap, which prevents #[derive(Parser)] from compiling.
Running cargo commands outside the newly created project folder.

steps.title: Define CLI struct and parse path
steps.instructions: In src/main.rs, define a struct deriving Debug and Parser with an optional PathBuf field named path, and call its ::parse() in main. Run `cargo run -- -h` to see the generated help.

targets.caption: Define the CLI struct with Option<PathBuf>
Check auto-generated help output from cargo run -- -h

explanations.topic: Passing CLI flags to cargo run using --
How clap auto-generates help text from struct fields

hints: Import Parser from clap and PathBuf from std::path.
Add #[derive(Debug, Parser)] above your struct containing path: Option<PathBuf>.
Call CLI::parse() in main() and run cargo run -- -h.
common_mistakes: Omitting -- before -h when calling cargo run, which passes -h to Cargo instead of your binary.
Forgetting to import clap::Parser or std::path::PathBuf.
steps.code: use clap::Parser; use std::path::PathBuf; #[derive(Debug, Parser)] struct CLI { path: Option<PathBuf>, } fn main() { let cli = CLI::parse(); println!("Hello, world!"); }

steps.title: Add command metadata and unwrap path
steps.instructions: Add #[command(version, about, long_about = ...)] to the CLI struct, then unwrap cli.path with a default of PathBuf::from(".") and print it. Run `cargo run -- longpath` to see the path echoed.

targets.caption: Add version, about, and long_about metadata to CLI
Default missing path argument to current directory
Run the binary with a path argument

explanations.topic: Adding version and long_about command attributes

hints: Place #[command(version, about, long_about = "...")] directly under #[derive(Debug, Parser)].
Use cli.path.unwrap_or(PathBuf::from(".")) to get a PathBuf.
Print path.display() and test with both cargo run -- --help and cargo run -- longpath.
common_mistakes: Using println!("{}", path) directly instead of path.display(), since PathBuf does not implement Display.
Forgetting to save src/main.rs before running cargo run.
steps.code: #[derive(Debug, Parser)] #[command(version, about, long_about = "Best Ls command ever")] struct CLI { path: Option<PathBuf>, } fn main() { let cli = CLI::parse(); let path = cli.path.unwrap_or(PathBuf::from(".")); println!("{}", path.display()); }

steps.title: Check path existence and color errors
steps.instructions: Add owo-colors = "4.2.1" to Cargo.toml and import owo_colors::OwoColorize and std::fs in src/main.rs. Replace the print in main with fs::exists on your path and print "Path does not exist" in red when false.

targets.caption: Add owo-colors dependency
Check if the provided path exists

explanations.topic: Building and running executable from target/debug

hints: Add owo-colors = "4.2.1" under [dependencies] in Cargo.toml.
Use if let Ok(does_exist) = fs::exists(&path) to unwrap the Result<bool>.
Import OwoColorize so you can call .red() on string literals.
common_mistakes: Passing path by value to fs::exists(path) instead of &path, which moves path.
Forgetting to import owo_colors::OwoColorize, causing the .red() method to not be found.
steps.code: use owo_colors::OwoColorize; use std::fs; if let Ok(does_exist) = fs::exists(&path) { if does_exist { } else { println!("{}", "Path does not exist".red()); } }

steps.title: Read directory entries with get_files
steps.instructions: Handle the outer else branch of fs::exists with an error message, and create a get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String> function using fs::read_dir. Loop over get_files in main and print each entry.

targets.caption: Implement get_files using fs::read_dir
Iterate and print directory filenames

explanations.topic: Why fs::exists returns Result and handling errors

hints: Import Path from std::path alongside PathBuf.
Inside get_files, iterate fs::read_dir(path) and convert file.file_name().into_string().
Call get_files(&path) inside the if does_exist block and print each file.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to return data at the end of get_files (or adding a semicolon after data).
Not handling the Result from into_string() on OsString returned by file_name().
steps.code: use std::path::{Path, PathBuf}; if does_exist { for file in get_files(&path) { println!("{}", file); } } else { println!("{}", "Path does not exist".red()); } } else { println!("{}", "error reading directory".red()); } fn get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String> { let mut data = Vec::default(); if let Ok(read_dir) = fs::read_dir(path) { for entry in read_dir { if let Ok(file) = entry { data.push(file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into())); } } } data }

steps.title: Extract file metadata into FileEntry
steps.instructions: Add strum and strum_macros (0.27) to Cargo.toml, then define EntryType and FileEntry in src/main.rs. Update get_files to return Vec<FileEntry> filled via fs::metadata in a map_data helper.

targets.caption: Add strum and strum_macros crates
Create FileEntry struct and EntryType enum
Extract metadata mapping into map_data

explanations.topic: Using strum Display macro on enums
Fixing fs::metadata(&path) bug to use file.path()

hints: Add strum = { version = "0.27", features = ["derive"] } and strum_macros = "0.27" to Cargo.toml.
Use fs::metadata(file.path()) rather than fs::metadata(&path) so each entry gets its own size and type.
Print each FileEntry with {:?} in main to inspect the metadata.
common_mistakes: Passing &path instead of file.path() to fs::metadata, causing every entry to show the directory's metadata.
Forgetting to change the return type of get_files from Vec<String> to Vec<FileEntry>.
steps.code: #[derive(Debug, Display)] enum EntryType { File, Dir, } #[derive(Debug)] struct FileEntry { name: String, e_type: EntryType, len_btyes: u64, modified: String, } fn map_data(file: fs::DirEntry, data: &mut Vec<FileEntry>) { if let Ok(meta) = fs::metadata(file.path()) { data.push(FileEntry { name: file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into()), e_type: if meta.is_dir() { EntryType::Dir } else { EntryType::File }, len_btyes: meta.len(), modified: "".to_string(), }); } }

steps.title: Format output as colored ASCII table
steps.instructions: Add tabled = "0.20.0" to Cargo.toml, derive Tabled on your FileEntry struct with #[tabled(rename = ...)] header attributes, then build a Table in main with Style::rounded() and column/row colors. Run cargo run to see the table.

targets.caption: Add tabled crate to Cargo.toml
Build, style, and print the tabled::Table

explanations.topic: Rendering structs as tables with tabled
Renaming table columns with tabled attributes

hints: Import Table, Tabled, and settings::{object::{Columns, Rows}, Color, Style} from tabled.
Call table.with(Style::rounded()) and table.modify(...) for column and header row colors.
Use #[tabled(rename = "Size B")] above struct fields to customize header labels.
common_mistakes: Importing Style from clap or owo_colors instead of tabled::settings::Style.
Forgetting to mark table as mut before calling .with() and .modify().
steps.code: #[derive(Debug, Tabled)] struct FileEntry { #[tabled(rename = "Name")] name: String, #[tabled(rename = "Type")] e_type: EntryType, #[tabled(rename = "Size B")] len_btyes: u64, modified: String, } let mut table = Table::new(get_files); table.with(Style::rounded()); table.modify(Columns::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_CYAN); table.modify(Columns::one(2), Color::FG_BRIGHT_MAGENTA); table.modify(Rows::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_GREEN); println!("{}", table);

steps.title: Format modification dates with chrono
steps.instructions: Add chrono = "0.4.41" to Cargo.toml and import DateTime and Utc in src/main.rs. In map_data, convert meta.modified() into DateTime<Utc>, format it with "%a %b %e %Y", and set the Size B column color to FG_BRIGHT_YELLOW.

targets.caption: Add chrono crate for date formatting
Convert SystemTime to DateTime<Utc> and format it
Run cargo run -- src to see dates

explanations.topic: Converting SystemTime from metadata into chrono DateTime<Utc>

hints: Add chrono = "0.4.41" to Cargo.toml and use chrono::{DateTime, Utc}; in src/main.rs.
Avoid naming the variable mod since it is a Rust keyword; use modi instead.
Use date.format("%a %b %e %Y") inside format!("{}", ...).
common_mistakes: Naming the variable mod in if let Ok(mod), which causes a syntax error because mod is a reserved Rust keyword.
Forgetting the else branch when constructing the modified String field.
steps.code: use chrono::{DateTime, Utc}; modified: if let Ok(modi) = meta.modified() { let date: DateTime<Utc> = modi.into(); format!("{}", date.format("%a %b %e %Y")) } else { String::default() }

steps.title: Add json flag and serde serialization
steps.instructions: Add serde (with derive) and serde_json to Cargo.toml, derive Serialize on your entry structs/enums, and add #[arg(short, long)] json: bool to the CLI struct. Print serde_json::to_string of the files when --json is passed, then run cargo run -- -j.

targets.caption: Add serde and serde_json dependencies
Add -j / --json boolean flag to CLI struct
Serialize directory entries to JSON when --json is set

explanations.topic: Adding short and long CLI flags with clap

hints: Add serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] } and serde_json = "1.0" to Cargo.toml.
Derive Serialize on both FileEntry and EntryType.
Add #[arg(short, long)] above json: bool in CLI so clap treats it as a flag rather than a positional argument.
common_mistakes: Adding json: bool without #[arg(short, long)], which makes clap treat it as a required positional argument.
Deriving Serialize on FileEntry without also deriving Serialize on EntryType.
steps.code: #[arg(short, long)] json: bool, if cli.json { let get_files = get_files(&path); println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&get_files).unwrap_or("cannot parse json".to_string())); } else { print_table(path); }
